summary: Initialized active v2 Bootstrap Planning Ledger for exact placeholder feature token `<provider updates>`, registered it in ledger_registry.json, captured the collaborator planning persona and ledger-only constraints, and opened q-0001 to ask what we are working on before accepting product requirements.

Jared clarified that provider Plans need currentness updates, starting with Gemini CLI being deprecated/replaced by Antigravity CLI (`agy`) and Antigravity CLI supporting multiple models. Live Google transition docs, the official google-antigravity/antigravity-cli repo at 5a7b8ef88e99e62a4d68a7cdf056c21a5fcc2d53, the installer manifest for 1.0.11, changelog, README, and Google codelab/docs content were inspected. Findings were recorded ledger-only with open migration/model/account questions before canonical Plans edits.

Jared corrected the Antigravity direction: Gemini CLI support should be killed and replaced by Antigravity, not preserved as an enterprise compatibility path; provider modeling should follow provider -> models like OpenCode, allowing the same model to appear under multiple providers; account isolation/home override assumptions from Gemini CLI do not work; and thinking effort level selection must apply across all providers and models. Antigravity CLI 1.0.11 was installed into /tmp, non-authenticated commands were verified, and authenticated model/prompt commands were confirmed auth-gated.

Jared clarified that Gemini Direct API is OK to keep, so the Gemini deletion scope is Gemini CLI and stale CLI/media helper assumptions rather than direct Gemini API. He also expanded the provider update to media support and OpenAI(ChatGPT/codex) `ChatGPT 2 image generation`; official OpenAI ChatGPT Images 2.0, GPT Image 2, API image-generation, Codex app/CLI/IDE image-generation, C2PA/SynthID, rate-limit, and org-verification docs were researched and recorded as ledger-only source lineage.

Jared asked for the assistant recommendation, required research into which providers support other media, and asked what authenticated verification meant. The ledger recorded a candidate recommendation to model provider entries by execution/auth/billing boundary with optional provider-family UI grouping, expanded media research scope to image/video/TTS/audio/music, recorded first-pass official/current provider media support findings, clarified authenticated verification as signed-in/API-key route probes before exact command/API behavior is canonicalized, and kept all work ledger-only without editing canonical Plans.

Jared accepted the execution/auth/billing-boundary provider taxonomy but clarified that OpenAI was only an example and the same provider-family/grouping rule applies to other vendors too. Jared also answered `Both` for coding-plan versus general media provider routes: PM should preserve coding-plan providers and also add separate general media API provider routes where vendors support media, rather than merging those surfaces.

Jared closed the verification-threshold question: there should be no uncertainty, providers should be tested locally to make sure they work as expected, direct providers can use the pulled OpenCode repo for inspection, and CLI providers must be tested by the assistant. The active Anomaly OpenCode repo was cloned at bcff162c60772aeccc8c6bbcf229da406a07eae5 and inspected for provider/model catalog, modalities, and thinking-variant behavior. Local sanitized CLI probes were run for Antigravity, Cursor Agent, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot through gh, and OpenCode CLI presence, producing an explicit compile blocker for incomplete/failing CLI provider verification. No canonical Plans or generated governance artifacts were edited.

Jared corrected the local verification scope: Codex and OpenCode are direct providers, so PM does not need to bridge their CLIs for core provider support. Follow-up isolated installs/probes were recorded: current `@openai/codex@0.142.2` executed a minimal prompt and accepted low reasoning-effort config, `opencode-ai@1.17.11` installed the `opencode` command, `@opencode-ai/cli@1.17.11` installed the v2-preview `lildax` command, Cursor update remained unauthenticated, Claude prompt mode still reported not logged in, GitHub Copilot prompt still exited non-zero, and Antigravity remained auth-gated with no local gcloud ADC. Blocker `blk-0001` was narrowed to active CLI-bridged routes only; Codex/OpenCode CLI issues are evidence only unless optional CLI tooling is later requested.

Follow-up probes refined the active CLI-bridged blocker set after Codex/OpenCode were excluded: `USE_ADC=1 agy models` still returned sign-in-required and local `gcloud` was not found; Cursor Agent `about` reported `User Email Not logged in`, `models` returned no models, and update returned unauthenticated; current Claude Code prompt mode returned `Not logged in` despite auth status, and `claude doctor` did not return before manual interruption; GitHub Copilot CLI through `gh` still exited `1` for a minimal prompt with no useful response. These are account/auth/runtime readiness blockers for active CLI bridges, not product questions.

Jared asked whether the only blocker for CLI providers is that they are not logged in. The ledger classification was clarified: the remaining active CLI-bridge blockers are primarily account/auth/entitlement/session readiness rather than missing installation or command-surface blockers, but they should not all be simplified to plain `not logged in`. Antigravity needs sign-in or configured ADC, Cursor has inconsistent account/model readiness, Claude non-interactive prompt auth does not match auth status, and GitHub Copilot through `gh` has GitHub auth present but prompt execution still exits 1 with no useful output.

Jared asked for deeper GitHub Copilot CLI research and whether `Nomadcxx/opencode-cursor`, `standardagents/composer-api`, or the Cursor SDK provide a better Cursor support approach. Current `@github/copilot@1.0.65` was installed in /tmp and probed: it exposes reasoning-effort, output-format, mode, attachment, and BYOK/custom-provider surfaces, but hosted prompt execution returns `Access denied by policy settings` / `403 unauthorized`, making the blocker policy/subscription/license/admin enablement. `opencode-cursor` was cloned at 21631ec9b05bc4ac02eb734e1a742a3a9e48e0d3 and recorded as useful OpenCode-specific source-lineage but not PM's primary Cursor route because it defaults to `cursor-agent` when available. `composer-api` was cloned at f90f45c39e3e72065d41cf661ac17416bf6ae978 and recorded as the stronger primary Cursor SDK/local OpenAI-compatible route candidate, with text/image input and explicit unsupported-feature notes, but local runtime verification remains blocked because no Cursor API key or local API server was available.

Jared asked to test the Cursor approaches if possible. Raw `cursor-agent` was tested directly: status remains inconsistent and both text and stream-json headless prompts fail with `Authentication required`. `opencode-cursor` was installed in a temp prefix and then tested with isolated OpenCode config: it can install provider config and generate a fallback 14-model catalog, but runtime prompts surface Cursor auth errors while OpenCode exits 0, so PM must inspect output/errors rather than process exit alone. A brief accidental write to the user's OpenCode config was identified as test-created and removed, restoring provider disabled/missing state. `composer-api` was tested from the repo: `npm install`, `npm test` (9 files / 227 tests), and `npm run typecheck` passed; its standalone Cursor SDK bridge starts and returns expected 400/401 key-gated errors; Vite dev-server probing is blocked by Cloudflare container/Docker setup, and Swift package tests were interrupted after Sparkle artifact download stalled. No Cursor route has live completion proof without a real Cursor API key/local app session.

Jared challenged whether Cursor uses OAuth logins rather than an API. Current Cursor docs, local `cursor-agent --help`, and the pulled Cursor bridge repos show a route-specific auth model: normal Cursor app / interactive Cursor Agent CLI uses browser-login/OAuth-style session auth; Cursor Agent headless scripting can use `--api-key` or `CURSOR_API_KEY`; Cursor SDK, Cursor REST/API, Cloud Agents, and `composer-api` local OpenAI-compatible bridge routes require user/service-account API-key auth; `opencode-cursor` is hybrid source-lineage evidence. The ledger now forbids API-key-only and OAuth-only Cursor wording, while leaving Cursor live-completion blockers open.

Jared corrected the Cursor priority: `We should be focused on the oauth method, not the api.` The ledger now supersedes the prior Cursor SDK/local API primary-route preference. Cursor app / interactive Cursor Agent CLI browser-login/session auth is the primary route to verify and later compile. Cursor SDK/API-key/local OpenAI-compatible bridge evidence remains secondary, fallback, or source-lineage unless Jared explicitly promotes it, and lack of API-key proof must not block OAuth-focused Cursor support.

Jared was at the machine and asked to retry automated tests. Cursor Agent OAuth login completed successfully. Direct `cursor-agent` OAuth/session support is now live-verified: status/about show the redacted logged-in account, model listing returns 139 rows, text prompt returns exactly `cursor-oauth-ok`, and stream-json prompt returns `apiKeySource: login`, success subtype, `is_error: false`, and result `cursor-oauth-json-ok`. Retesting `opencode-cursor` showed it remains blocked: isolated HOME hides the session and fails auth, model sync falls back to 14 models because it cannot parse the live model output, and real-HOME/temp-config runs hang until interrupted. No long-running provider processes remained.

Jared said `claude`, interpreted in the active provider-testing thread as retrying Claude Code. Local Claude Code is installed at version 2.1.49 and auth status reports logged-in first-party `claude.ai` auth with redacted account details. JSON prompt using `claude -p --output-format json --permission-mode plan --tools "" --model sonnet` succeeded with result `claude-ok`. Stream-json initially failed because print-mode stream-json requires `--verbose`; rerun with `--verbose --effort low` succeeded with result `claude-stream-low-ok`. Effort selector probes for `--effort medium` and `--effort high` also succeeded. `claude doctor` still fails in non-interactive execution with Ink raw-mode error, so PM should use print-mode prompt probes rather than doctor as the provider readiness gate. No long-running Claude processes remained.

Jared said Claude Code, Antigravity, and Cursor are logged in now and asked to test them, plus test the OpenCode server as a direct provider. Fresh local probes confirmed Claude Code first-party `claude.ai` auth and prompt execution (`claude-retest-ok`) plus `--effort low`; Cursor Agent OAuth/session prompt execution returned `cursor-retest-ok` and help/models expose effort through parameterized model syntax and low/high/xhigh model variants; Antigravity CLI `agy` 1.0.12 now lists models and returns exact prompt markers for default, explicit `Gemini 3.5 Flash (Low)`, and explicit `Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking)` selections. OpenCode server 1.17.11 was started on localhost, health/API/catalog endpoints were inspected, and HTTP session/message prompt execution through `opencode/big-pickle` returned `opencode-server-ok`. OpenCode-server-routed `github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5` is catalog-visible but live prompt execution returned no text and server logs showed `AI_APICallError: Forbidden`, so it remains blocked. The server process was stopped after testing.

Jared clarified that `GitHub copilot likely isn’t working because I don’t have an active subscription.` The Copilot blocker is therefore recorded as likely subscription/entitlement-gated, consistent with the prior hosted CLI policy/subscription/license/admin denial and OpenCode-server-routed GitHub Copilot `AI_APICallError: Forbidden`. This is a user-supplied likely cause, not an externally verified billing-state inspection.

Jared asked where Cursor stands and what approach PM is taking. The ledger status was restated: primary Cursor route is direct Cursor Agent OAuth/browser-login/session auth through `cursor-agent`, already live-verified with status/about, 139-model catalog, text prompt, stream-json prompt, and fresh retest. `opencode-cursor` is not the primary route and remains blocked/hanging with parser fallback behavior. Cursor SDK/API/composer-api/local bridge work remains secondary/fallback/source-lineage unless explicitly promoted and still needs API-key/local-app completion proof if compiled as its own route.

Jared asked whether Cursor is locked in and whether there is a fleshed-out plan to make it work. The ledger records yes for the primary Cursor route: direct `cursor-agent` OAuth/browser-login/session support is locked as the compile target, using `cursor-agent models` for provider-owned catalog, `cursor-agent --print --trust --mode ask` for prompt execution, stream-json/text output handling, model IDs and parameterized syntax for thinking-effort selection, and local prompt/catalog/status gates for support claims. `opencode-cursor` and SDK/API/composer-api/local bridge routes remain secondary/fallback/source-lineage and must not block the primary route.

Jared challenged the Cursor route: the locked direct `cursor-agent` route is a CLI bridge, not ACP, and `standardagents/composer-api` may be more feature complete because it uses a Cursor Dashboard -> Integrations API key tied to the Cursor subscription. Current research/probes confirmed: `agent acp` exists and a minimal ACP JSON-RPC prompt returned `cursor-acp-ok`; current composer-api repo exposes local OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/models`, uses a Cursor user API key stored locally in a macOS app, supports streaming and image input, and configures OpenCode against the local base URL. The local composer-api app/server is not currently installed/running on port 8787, so live completion still needs a real API key/app proof. Recommendation recorded: promote composer-api from secondary fallback to preferred direct-provider candidate contingent on local verification, keep ACP as first-party session/agent route, and demote print-mode `cursor-agent` to fallback.

Jared provided a Cursor API key for live testing and explicitly said not to put it in the ledger. The key was not recorded in ledger files. Current composer-api repo commit `f90f45c39e3e72065d41cf661ac17416bf6ae978` was pulled and tested. Direct `@cursor/sdk` model discovery returned 31 models and a local-agent prompt returned exactly `cursor-api-sdk-ok`. The standalone Responses proxy verified `/v1/models`, non-streaming `/v1/responses`, response retrieval, streaming Responses SSE, and image input with a red PNG returning `red`. The local-agent bridge verified non-streaming text, NDJSON streaming, and client-tool forwarding through SDK MCP. The Worker/Vite `/v1` surface, run from the temp clone with external bridge config, verified models, chat completions, chat streaming, Responses create/retrieve, and chat tool calls. Repo `npm test` passed 9 files / 227 tests and `npm run typecheck` passed. Cursor native API-key/SDK/composer-api-style route is now live-verified for planning; `opencode-cursor` remains non-primary because PM has native support and OpenCode needs the plugin for Cursor.

Jared asked whether Claude Code v2.1.80 status-line `rate_limits` is an issue PM needs to address, and asked to update coding-plan support including Qwen coding and Kimi while checking whether OpenCode uses default OpenAI provider settings. Official Claude Code status-line docs confirm `rate_limits.five_hour.used_percentage`, `rate_limits.five_hour.resets_at`, `rate_limits.seven_day.used_percentage`, and `rate_limits.seven_day.resets_at` in status-line stdin JSON, with graceful absence handling required. A local `claude -p` print-mode status-line probe did not trigger statusLine and an interactive PTY probe did not produce durable capture evidence, so planning relies on official docs plus Reddit source-lineage. OpenCode current repo and live Models.dev were inspected: OpenCode uses Models.dev plus generic `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` or other AI SDK provider paths with configured base URLs/body/header fragments, not first-party OpenAI defaults and not provider-specific behavior that is absent from config. Live coding-plan source-lineage now includes Alibaba/Qwen, Kimi, Z.AI/Zhipu, Tencent, MiniMax, KUAE, and Umans routes with provider/model/media metadata. Qwen Code docs/source confirm Alibaba ModelStudio Coding Plan region endpoints, `BAILIAN_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY`, versioned model templates, and `extra_body: { enable_thinking: true }`. Kimi For Coding parity requires provider-specific auth/client-identity, `prompt_cache_key`, thinking/reasoning mapping, `/coding/v1/models` discovery, and media metadata, with a recorded caution not to silently forge/tamper client identity. No canonical Plans or governance artifacts were edited.

Jared asked whether the newest OpenCode repo had been pulled and inspected specifically for first-class coding-plan providers because PM will need to implement them. `/tmp/pm-opencode-current` was refreshed from `https://github.com/sst/opencode`; it was current with `origin/dev` at commit `b60c0a5e8ccc71ef7cce327602401418d419472e` (`2026-06-25T19:09:22Z`, package version `1.17.11`). Inspection confirmed OpenCode treats coding-plan IDs as first-class provider/catalog entries mostly through Models.dev ingestion plus generic AI SDK provider plugins and `ProviderTransform` rules, not dedicated adapter files per coding-plan provider. Live Models.dev was re-queried at `2026-06-25T20:04:49Z` and confirmed provider IDs, env keys, endpoints, SDK package choices, model counts, and media examples for Alibaba/Qwen, Kimi, Z.AI/Zhipu, Tencent, MiniMax, KUAE, and Umans coding-plan providers. Important implementation caution recorded: stock OpenCode currently sets DashScope `enable_thinking: true` only for `alibaba-cn`, not `alibaba-coding-plan` or `alibaba-coding-plan-cn`; PM therefore needs its own coding-plan-specific transform mapping and E2E tests rather than blindly copying stock OpenCode behavior. No canonical Plans or governance artifacts were edited.

Jared clarified that much of the provider-adjacent audit is already addressed in the new provider-update ledger and asked to work through only the items not already addressed, then reminded the assistant to work only in the ledger. The audit findings in `Plans/.audits/audit-20260625-001-provider-adjacent-plans/` were reconciled against existing accepted atoms/decisions. Covered findings include Gemini CLI retirement/Antigravity replacement, Provider -> models taxonomy, Cursor route hierarchy, media matrix direction, OpenCode direct-provider/source-lineage handling, coding-plan provider expansion, thinking-effort support, and Claude Code rate_limits. New ledger-only deltas were recorded for provider launcher/BinaryLocator metadata, caller-scoped capability schemas, account-bound GUI model selectors, requested/effective account resolution, provider-native tool permission/secret boundaries, runtime artifact schemas, provider usage source confidence, and stale-anchor retirement. No canonical Plans, audit files, generated governance artifacts, shards, evidence, plan graph, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, or executable queues were edited.
